subtitle: How Mummadi Turned a Palace into a Living Library of Images

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide inside a dim palace hall lined with manuscripts and paintings
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits cross-legged on a carved platform in Mysore Palace, surrounded by open illuminated folios and hanging paintings that glow in lamplight, court artists frozen mid-brush around him.

dialogue.text: In a Mysore watched by Company officers and priests, Krishnaraja Wodeyar III built a different fortress — a palace where gods, games and yoga were painted, named and saved in the Sritattvanidhi.

i18n.hi: कंपनी अफ़सरों और पुजारियों की निगरानी वाले मैसूर में, कृष्णराज वोडेयार तृतीय ने अलग किला रचा — एक महल, जहाँ देवता, खेल और योग चित्रों में रँगकर, नाम पाकर ‘श्रीतत्त्वनिधि’ में सँभाले गए।

panels.shot: slow push-in from balcony high above the Mysore Palace courtyard
panels.action: A young Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, in simple royal robes, leans over a balcony of Mysore Palace, looking down at British officers and Mysore courtiers conferring in the courtyard below.

dialogue.text: Restored as a child to a reduced throne, Krishnaraja Wodeyar III ruled under British supervision, between old ritual and new empire, searching for a space where his power could be his own.

i18n.hi: बचपन में घटे हुए सिंहासन पर लौटाए गए कृष्णराज वोडेयार तृतीय ने अंग्रेज़ निगरानी में, पुराने रिवाज़ और नए साम्राज्य के बीच, अपना सचमुच का अधिकार खोजने की कोशिश की।

panels.shot: medium interior shot at a writing desk lit by a single oil lamp
panels.action: Older Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits at a low desk in an inner chamber, surrounded by palm-leaf bundles and paper manuscripts, as a palace scribe kneels nearby awaiting dictation.

dialogue.text: Unlike warriors before him, Mummadi turned inward. The court became his workshop, his weapons ink and brush, his ambition to capture a kingdom of memory between covers.

i18n.hi: पहले के वीरों से अलग, मुम्मडी भीतर की ओर मुड़े। दरबार उनका कार्यशाला बना, कलम और कूची उनके हथियार, और महत्वाकांक्षा — यादों का एक राज्य किताबों के बीच कैद करना।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close-up of a manuscript folio being opened
panels.action: From behind Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, we see his hands gently opening a thick illustrated manuscript folio, revealing bright, carefully drawn figures of deities and Sanskrit-Kannada headings.

dialogue.text: From this urge was born the Sritattvanidhi, a grand Kannada compendium. Not a poem, not a single scripture, but a treasury where pictures and words marched together in disciplined rows.

i18n.hi: इसी तड़प से जन्मी ‘श्रीतत्त्वनिधि’ — भव्य कन्नड़ ग्रंथ। न केवल कविता, न कोई एक धर्मग्रंथ, बल्कि एक ख़ज़ाना, जहाँ तस्वीर और शब्द क़तार में, अनुशासन से साथ-साथ चलते हैं।

panels.shot: bird's-eye view of a palace studio with multiple artists at work
panels.action: Inside a spacious Jagan Mohan Palace atelier, rows of court painters sit on the floor, carefully copying and coloring deity forms while Krishnaraja Wodeyar III walks among them, observing with keen interest.

dialogue.text: Mysore already had painters and priests. Mummadi gave them a manual. Each image in the Sritattvanidhi fixed posture, ornament and color, a reference for every artist in his kingdom.

i18n.hi: मैसूर में चित्रकार और पुजारी पहले से थे। मुम्मडी ने उन्हें मार्गदर्शिका दी। ‘श्रीतत्त्वनिधि’ की हर तसवीर में आसन, गहना और रंग तय, ताकि उनके राज्य का हर कलाकार एक ही मिसाल देख सके।

panels.shot: tight close-up on a painter’s hand finishing an icon
panels.action: A palace painter’s steady hand applies final color to a carefully outlined god on the page, while Krishnaraja Wodeyar III’s finger points to a margin note beside it.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii
dialogue.text: The hand may change, but the form must stay true.

i18n.hi: हाथ बदल सकते हैं, पर रूप सच्चा रहना चाहिए।

dialogue.text: The compendium did not invent new gods; it disciplined their faces, weapons and moods, so that Mysore’s images followed one shared memory instead of many scattered habits.

i18n.hi: इस ग्रंथ ने नए देवता नहीं गढ़े; उसने उनके चेहरे, हथियार और भाव सँवारे, ताकि मैसूर की तस्वीरें बिखरी आदतों की जगह साझा स्मृति का रूप लें।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king watching dancers and priests in a temple hall
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits on a low throne in a temple-like hall as priests, musicians and dancers perform before carved icons, the light of camphor lamps flickering on their faces.

dialogue.text: Outside the pages, ritual went on in halls and shrines. Inside the pages, he tried to catch its order — which god stood how, which symbol meant what, so that practice and painting could speak the same language.

i18n.hi: किताब के बाहर, हॉल और मंदिरों में पूजा चलती रही। पन्नों के भीतर, उसने उसका अनुशासन पकड़ा — कौन देवता कैसे खड़े, कौन चिह्न क्या कहे, ताकि साधना और चित्र एक ही भाषा बोलें।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a quiet chamber with drawn yoga postures on the floor
panels.action: In a secluded palace room, Krishnaraja Wodeyar III kneels over large sheets spread on the floor, each bearing a neatly drawn figure in a different yoga posture, while a court scholar explains from a palm-leaf text.

dialogue.text: One section of the Sritattvanidhi went further. It pictured human bodies in yoga postures, joining older textual lists with the eye of a painter, making a bridge between practice, instruction and image.

i18n.hi: ‘श्रीतत्त्वनिधि’ का एक भाग और आगे बढ़ा। उसने योगासन में मानव देह को दिखाया, पुराने ग्रंथों की सूचियों को चित्रकार की नज़र से जोड़ते हुए, साधना, शिक्षा और चित्र के बीच पुल बनाया।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of the king watching a court yogi hold a posture
panels.action: A court yogi holds a steady asana on a mat in front of Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, while the king compares the posture to a drawn figure held in his hand.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii
dialogue.text: The line must remember the body as it truly stands.

i18n.hi: रेखाओं को शरीर की असली मुद्रा याद रखनी होगी।

dialogue.text: Later scholars would mine these drawings to trace Mysore’s yoga tradition, but in his own day they were part of the same urge — to see, to name, to file away for those yet to come.

i18n.hi: आगे चलकर विद्वान इन्हीं चित्रों से मैसूर की योग परंपरा के सूत्र खोजेंगे, पर उनके समय में ये उसी चाह के हिस्से थे — देखना, नाम देना, और आने वालों के लिए सहेजकर रखना।

panels.shot: wide shot of a palace room filled with games and painted boards
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, relaxed and smiling, sits among courtiers in a room where painted board games, dice and illustrated manuals lie scattered, while a palace artist sketches one of the boards.

dialogue.text: The treasury did not stop at gods and postures. It turned to games and pastimes, recording boards and pieces, showing how a king who could not fight great wars still commanded a battlefield of leisure and intellect.

i18n.hi: यह ख़ज़ाना देवताओं और आसनों पर नहीं रुका। यह खेलों और मनबहलाव की ओर भी मुड़ा, बिसात और गोटियाँ दर्ज करते हुए, दिखाता रहा कि जो राजा बड़े युद्ध न लड़ सका, वह भी अवकाश और बुद्धि के मैदान पर सेनानायक था।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of king and scribe in discussion at a desk
panels.action: By lamplight, Krishnaraja Wodeyar III confers with a senior court scholar and scribe at a manuscript-strewn desk, pointing toward a stack labeled with neat cloth wraps.

dialogue.text: To gather such variety, Mummadi needed more than artists. He drew on priests, artisans, yogis and scholars, weaving court knowledge into one organized palace book instead of many jealous, private memories.

i18n.hi: इतना वैविध्य जुटाने को मुम्मडी को सिर्फ़ चित्रकार नहीं चाहिए थे। उन्होंने पुजारी, कारीगर, योगी और विद्वान जोड़े, दरबारी ज्ञान को अलग‑अलग निजी यादों की बजाय एक संगठित महल‑ग्रंथ में पिरो दिया।

panels.shot: slow tracking shot along shelves of manuscripts in a later archive
panels.action: Rows of bound manuscripts rest in wooden cupboards of the Oriental Research Institute, with one open folio of the Sritattvanidhi displayed on a stand, its colors still vivid under soft light.

dialogue.text: Long after Mummadi was gone, the Sritattvanidhi lay in palace and institutional custody. When modern researchers opened its folios in Mysore’s Oriental Research Institute, they found a king’s mind arranged in pigments and script.

i18n.hi: मुम्मडी के बाद भी ‘श्रीतत्त्वनिधि’ महल और संस्थानों की सभाल में रहा। जब आधुनिक शोधकर्ताओं ने मैसूर के ओरिएंटल रिसर्च इंस्टीट्यूट में उसके पन्ने खोले, उन्हें एक राजा की सोच रंग और अक्षरों में सजी मिली।

panels.shot: medium shot of a modern scholar studying the manuscript
panels.action: A modern scholar sits at a table in the Oriental Research Institute, carefully studying and taking notes from an open Sritattvanidhi yoga folio.

dialogue.text: Norman Sjoman and others would later trace lines of yoga teaching through these painted bodies and annotations. The compendium, once a working palace manual, became a key to Mysore’s contribution to modern yoga history.

i18n.hi: बाद में नॉर्मन स्योमन और दूसरे विद्वानों ने इन्हीं आकृतियों और टिप्पणियों से योग की शिक्षाओं की रेखाएँ खोजीं। जो ग्रंथ कभी महल की कामकाजी पुस्तिका था, वही आधुनिक योग इतिहास में मैसूर के योगदान की कुंजी बना।

panels.shot: medium shot of Krishnaraja Wodeyar III listening to a court poet in a decorated hall
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits attentively in a decorated hall as a Jain court poet, Devachandra, recites from a palm-leaf manuscript, courtiers listening in respectful silence.

dialogue.text: Text alone still had its place. Under his patronage, Devachandra’s Rajavali Katha retold Mysore’s past in Kannada, stitching dynastic memory and legend into a court chronicle that later historians would carefully test and use.

i18n.hi: सिर्फ़ लिखित पाठ की भी अपनी जगह रही। उनके संरक्षण में देवचंद्र की ‘राजावली कथा’ ने मैसूर के अतीत को कन्नड़ में दोहराया, वंश‑स्मृति और कथा को जोड़कर ऐसा दरबारी वृत्तांत रचा, जिसे आगे के इतिहासकारों ने जाँचकर अपनाया।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of the king marking a passage in the chronicle
panels.action: From behind Krishnaraja Wodeyar III, we see his hand marking a passage in a freshly copied Rajavali Katha while attendants hold other volumes ready.

dialogue.speaker: krishnaraja_wodeyar_iii
dialogue.text: If our story is not written, others will write it for us.

i18n.hi: अगर हमारी कहानी हम नहीं लिखेंगे, तो कोई और हमारे लिए लिख देगा।

dialogue.text: Rajavali Katha did not give a neutral record; it gave a Mysore voice. In an age when colonial pens described his land, Mummadi made sure his court’s version also survived.

i18n.hi: ‘राजावली कथा’ सूखी, तटस्थ रिपोर्ट नहीं थी; वह मैसूर की आवाज़ थी। जब उपनिवेशी कलमें उसकी भूमि लिख रही थीं, मुम्मडी ने अपने दरबार का संस्करण भी सुरक्षित रखा।

panels.shot: wide shot of Jagan Mohan Palace facade with artists and students entering
panels.action: Outside Jagan Mohan Palace, artists and young students walk up the steps carrying portfolios and boards, as an older Krishnaraja Wodeyar III watches from a shaded balcony.

dialogue.text: Jagan Mohan Palace became more than a residence. It housed the ateliers and, later, collections that kept Mysore painting alive, with the Sritattvanidhi as silent tutor behind many a canvas.

i18n.hi: जаган मोहना महल महज़ आवास नहीं रहा। वहीं कार्यशालाएँ और बाद में संग्रह बने, जिन्होंने मैसूर चित्रकला को ज़िंदा रखा, और ‘श्रीतत्त्वनिधि’ अनगिनत कैनवसों के पीछे मौन गुरु बना रहा।

panels.shot: introspective close-up on the king’s face in old age
panels.action: In his old age, Krishnaraja Wodeyar III sits by a window, holding a worn manuscript, his face thoughtful as he gazes past it toward the city beyond the palace walls.

dialogue.text: He could not recover the full sovereignty of his ancestors. Yet by arranging images and narratives, Mummadi shaped how Mysore would remember itself, long after imperial flags had changed above its fort.

i18n.hi: वह अपने पूर्वजों की पूर्ण सत्ता वापस न ला सके। पर चित्र और कथाएँ क्रम में सजाकर, मुम्मडी ने तय किया कि मैसूर खुद को कैसे याद करेगा, बहुत बाद तक, जब क़िले के ऊपर साम्राज्य के झंडे बदल चुके होंगे।

panels.shot: composed split-scene showing palace past and archive present
panels.action: On one side, a ghosted image of Krishnaraja Wodeyar III oversees painters in his palace; on the other, a modern conservator gently turns the same painted folios in a climate-controlled room.

dialogue.text: Today his illuminated volumes demand careful, critical reading; legend, prescription and history intertwined. Yet they remind us of a simple, enduring act — a ruler turning his court into a workshop to guard knowledge against forgetting.

i18n.hi: आज उनकी चित्र‑पाण्डुलिपियाँ सावधान, आलोचनात्मक पढ़ाई माँगती हैं; कथा, नियम और इतिहास एक‑दूसरे में घुले हैं। पर वे हमें एक सीधी, टिकाऊ हरकत याद दिलाती हैं — एक शासक, जिसने अपने दरबार को कार्यशाला बनाकर ज्ञान को विस्मृति से बचाया।
